theysay.say: The Trinity is pagan — the word isn't even in the Bible.
theysay.quick: Neither is 'theocracy,' 'Governing Body,' or 'Bible' itself — the question is whether the *idea* is there, and Thomas calls Jesus 'my Lord and my God' in John 20:28 without being corrected. **Ask what Jesus meant in John 5:23: that all should honor the Son just as they honor the Father.**

theysay.say: Jesus is God's first creation — 'the firstborn of all creation.'
theysay.quick: In Scripture 'firstborn' is a rank, not a birth order — David is appointed 'firstborn' as the youngest son (Psalm 89:27). **The very next verse says ALL things were created through him and FOR him — which is why the NWT had to insert the word 'other' four times.**

theysay.say: Jesus died on a torture stake — the cross is a pagan symbol.
theysay.quick: Whatever the wood's shape, John 20:25 says nails (plural) through his hands, which fits a crossbeam, and no doctrine hangs on it. **Ask why the shape of the instrument matters more than the One who died on it.**

theysay.say: God's name Jehovah was removed from the New Testament by Christendom.
theysay.quick: There are over 5,000 ancient Greek New Testament manuscripts and not one contains the divine name — the NWT inserts 'Jehovah' 237 times with zero manuscript support. **The 'removal' theory asks you to believe God let his Word be corrupted — the exact thing Jesus denied in Matthew 24:35.**

theysay.say: Only 144,000 go to heaven — everyone else lives forever on a paradise earth.
theysay.quick: Revelation 7 also says they're male Jewish virgins from twelve named tribes — why is the number literal but everything else symbolic? **And Revelation 19:1 places the 'great crowd' IN heaven, standing before God's throne.**

theysay.say: Christmas and birthdays are pagan celebrations.
theysay.quick: Watchtower literature admits wedding rings likely have pagan roots yet allows them because present meaning is what counts — the same logic they refuse to apply to a child's birthday. **Ask why Romans 14:5-6 lets each Christian decide about days, but their organization decides for them.**

theysay.say: We're the only ones preaching the good news in all the earth.
theysay.quick: Bible translators, missionaries, and churches were taking the gospel worldwide centuries before 1879, and still dwarf JW output today. **The real claim underneath is that only their organization counts — ask who decided that, and when.**

theysay.say: Look around — we're clearly living in the last days since 1914.
theysay.quick: Their own founder taught 1914 would be the END of the world's rulership, not the start of invisible kingship — the date kept its prestige only by changing its meaning. **If the chronology behind 1914 rests on 607 BCE, why does every historian date Jerusalem's fall to 587?**

theysay.say: Jesus has been ruling invisibly from heaven since October 1914.
theysay.quick: An invisible enthronement that nobody could observe was announced only after the visible predictions for 1914 failed. **Jesus warned about exactly this: 'If anyone says to you, Look! He is in the inner rooms — do not believe it' (Matthew 24:26).**

theysay.say: Jerusalem was destroyed in 607 BCE — that's where the 2,520 years to 1914 start.
theysay.quick: Every line of evidence — Babylonian business tablets, astronomical diaries like VAT 4956, and all modern scholarship — puts it at 587/586 BCE; 607 exists only because 1914 needs it. **Move the start date and 1914 evaporates, and with it the organization's claim to be appointed in 1919.**

theysay.say: The light gets brighter — Proverbs 4:18 explains why our understanding changes.
theysay.quick: Light getting brighter reveals more of what was already true; it doesn't make organ transplants cannibalism in 1967 and acceptable in 1980, or the 'generation' mean five different things. **Ask gently: was it light from God when it was taught, or when it was reversed — because it can't be both.**

theysay.say: The faithful and discreet slave provides our spiritual food at the proper time.
theysay.quick: That's their name for the Governing Body, which teaches Jesus inspected all religions in 1919 and chose them — a claim with no evidence outside their own publications. **Ask what Jesus was inspecting: in 1919 they were still teaching the Great Pyramid measured the last days.**

theysay.say: The soul isn't immortal — the dead are conscious of nothing at all.
theysay.quick: Ecclesiastes describes life 'under the sun,' but Jesus tells the thief 'today you will be with me in Paradise' and Paul calls departing to be 'with Christ' far better (Philippians 1:23). **Ask why Jesus warned about One who can destroy 'both soul AND body' if soul just means body (Matthew 10:28).**

theysay.say: A God of love would never torture people in hellfire.
theysay.quick: Agree that caricatures deserve rejection — then note Jesus spoke of final judgment more than anyone, and annihilation isn't obviously more loving than justice. **The deeper issue is that in their system Jesus' own resurrection wasn't bodily — ask what they do with 'destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up... he was talking about the temple of his body' (John 2:19-21).**

theysay.say: The holy spirit is God's active force, like electricity — not a person.
theysay.quick: Electricity doesn't speak, teach, intercede, get grieved, or say 'set apart for me Barnabas and Saul' (Acts 13:2). **Ask who the 'he' is in John 16:13-14 who hears, speaks, and glorifies Jesus.**

theysay.say: Blood transfusion violates God's law — Acts 15 says abstain from blood.
theysay.quick: Acts 15 addresses eating blood at the table, and their own policy now permits fractions of every blood component — hemoglobin included — which is incoherent if blood itself is sacredly off-limits. **Ask whether the Sabbath principle applies: 'the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath' (Mark 2:27).**

theysay.say: Where were YOU taught the Bible? Someone had to teach you.
theysay.quick: Fair question — and it cuts both ways, because every JW doctrine arrives through one publishing corporation that forbids checking it against outside scholarship. **The Beroeans were praised for verifying the apostle Paul against Scripture (Acts 17:11) — ask if they're allowed to do that to the Watchtower.**

theysay.say: Christendom's churches blessed both sides of the world wars.
theysay.quick: Real failures happened and honest Christians grieve them — but the Watchtower quietly held associate NGO status with the United Nations from 1992 to 2001, the very 'wild beast' it damns others for touching. **Institutional hypocrisy is an argument against institutions claiming to be God's channel, not against Christ.**

theysay.say: Armageddon is right around the corner — this generation will not pass away.
theysay.quick: That 'generation' has been redefined at least four times — people alive in 1914, then those who understood it, then since 2010 two overlapping lifespans that can stretch past the 2040s. **Ask what kind of promise survives by redefining its terms every time it fails.**

theysay.say: Higher education is spiritually dangerous and shows lack of faith in the end coming soon.
theysay.quick: Generations of young Witnesses skipped university for a paradise promised within their parents' lifetimes — a real cost paid for dates that failed. **Ask who bears the loss when the organization's timeline moves and your twenties don't come back.**

theysay.say: We don't shun anyone — people are free to leave whenever they want.
theysay.quick: Their own August 2024 Watchtower renamed disfellowshipping 'removal from the congregation' while instructing members not to associate with the removed — including family outside the household. **Ask softly: if you woke up doubting tomorrow, could you say so out loud without losing your mother?**

theysay.say: The New World Translation is the most accurate Bible ever produced.
theysay.quick: Its translation committee was anonymous, and the one identified member, Fred Franz, had no degree in biblical Greek or Hebrew; Greek scholars across the spectrum reject renderings like 'a god' in John 1:1. **Ask which published Greek grammarian, not affiliated with the Watchtower, endorses it.**

lessons.t: The contact — doorstep, cart, or 'informal witnessing'
what: Goal is never conversation for its own sake: it's the 'return visit' — a reason to come back (a question left open, a piece of literature, a video on the tablet)
Cart witnessing is deliberately passive; publishers are trained to let you approach so the contact feels self-initiated
Everything said at this stage is scripted from the meeting workbook — objections you raise have pre-loaded answers
Success metric used to be hours logged; since November 2023 rank-and-file just tick a box, but pioneers still count every hour of this
lessons.ask: I'd love to talk — **before we start, is there any question I could ask that would be allowed to change your mind?**

what: The current course is 'Enjoy Life Forever! — An Interactive Bible Course' (2021), 60 lessons with embedded JW.org videos
You study the book, not the Bible: each point cites verses, but the book supplies the interpretation and the questions
The Bible used is the New World Translation, so contested renderings (John 1:1, Colossians 1:16-17) arrive pre-settled
By design the study produces commitments along the way — attending a meeting, praying to 'Jehovah,' dropping holidays — before doctrine is examined critically
lessons.ask: **Are we studying the Bible, or studying a book that tells me what the Bible means?** Could we do one session with just the Bible — any translation you like?

lessons.t: The meeting invitation — entering the social world
what: Two weekly meetings (midweek 'Life and Ministry,' weekend public talk + Watchtower study) plus instant warmth: greeters, meal invitations, everyone knows your name
The welcome is real and it is also conditional — the friendship deepens exactly in step with your progress in the study
Answers at the Watchtower study are read from the paragraph just studied; independent commentary from the floor is not the format
This is where 'the truth' vocabulary starts: the congregation is 'the truth,' everything outside is 'the world'
lessons.ask: Everyone here has been so kind — **would these friendships survive if I studied everything and concluded differently?**

lessons.t: Unbaptized publisher — behaving in before believing through
what: You begin door-to-door work before baptism, after elders approve your conduct and doctrinal answers
Life conformity comes now: quit birthdays, holidays, church, voting, and often old friendships; dress and grooming expectations apply
Young people hear higher education framed as spiritually risky; pioneering is held up as the wise career
You are now publicly identified with the organization at doors — the psychological cost of leaving rises with every doorbell
lessons.ask: **Why does the practice change come before the doctrine test?** In Acts, people examined the message first and were baptized on belief in Jesus, not after a probation of conduct.

what: Candidates review dozens of questions with elders from 'Organized to Do Jehovah's Will' before approval

In 1985 the public baptism vow was changed: the second question now identifies you 'as one of Jehovah's Witnesses in association with God's spirit-directed organization' — the organization replaced the holy spirit in the formula (Watchtower, June 1, 1985); the 2019 revision still reads 'in association with Jehovah's organization'
That wording is legally and socially load-bearing: baptism is what makes you shunnable if you later leave
Most candidates are congregation children or study students at the emotional peak of belonging
lessons.ask: Jesus said baptize in the name of the Father, the Son, and the holy spirit — **who edited the holy spirit out of the vow and put an organization in?**

what: Rhythm: two meetings weekly with preparation, field service, family worship evening, twice-yearly circuit assemblies and a three-day regional convention
Monthly activity report (a participation checkbox since November 2023 — for 103 years before that, hours); pioneers still log hour quotas
Standing is visible and graded: publisher, auxiliary pioneer, regular pioneer, ministerial servant, elder — and everyone knows who's 'irregular' or 'inactive'
Doubt has no safe outlet: questioning teachings aloud can become a judicial matter, so fatigue is performed as joy
lessons.ask: **If you stopped reporting, attending, and knocking — what part of God's love for you would remain?** That answer tells you what the system believes about grace.

proofs.v: John 14:28 — 'the Father is greater than I'
proofs.they: Jesus plainly says the Father is greater, so Jesus cannot be God or equal to him.
proofs.you: 'Greater' describes position, not nature — a king is greater than his ambassador without being more human. Jesus speaks during his voluntary humbling, having 'emptied himself' to become man (Philippians 2:6-7), and the same Gospel opens with 'the Word was God' and closes with Thomas saying 'my Lord and my God' — unrebuked. The verse compares the Son on earth with the Father in glory, which is why Jesus is talking about *returning* to that glory (John 17:5).

proofs.they: Firstborn means first-created: Jesus is God's first and greatest creature, who then made everything else.
proofs.you: 'Firstborn' (prototokos) is a title of rank: David, the youngest son, is 'appointed firstborn' (Psalm 89:27), and Israel is God's 'firstborn' among nations it didn't precede. The context settles it — 'ALL things were created in him... through him and for him' (v.16) and 'he is before all things' (v.17). The New World Translation had to insert the word 'other' four times ('all other things') — unbracketed in 1950, bracketed 1961-1984, unbracketed again in 2013 — because without it the passage teaches exactly what they deny.

proofs.they: Exactly 144,000 anointed ones go to heaven to rule with Christ; the 'great crowd' of verse 9 lives forever on earth.
proofs.you: Read the whole passage: the 144,000 are also male virgins (14:4) from twelve named tribes of Israel — a list that oddly omits Dan and doubles Joseph, a signal of symbolism. Nobody takes the tribes, the maleness, or the celibacy literally; only the number, because the two-class system needs it. Meanwhile the great crowd stands 'before the throne' serving 'in his temple' (naos — the heavenly sanctuary, 7:15), and Revelation 19:1 explicitly locates 'a great crowd IN HEAVEN.'

proofs.they: God's personal name is Jehovah, and true worshippers must use it — churches hid it.
proofs.you: Using God's revealed name is wonderful — 'Jehovah' itself is a 16th-century hybrid of the Hebrew consonants YHWH with the vowels of 'Adonai,' so their 'restored' name is itself a later convention ('Yahweh' is closer). The decisive fact is the New Testament: not one of the 5,000+ Greek manuscripts contains the divine name, yet the NWT inserts 'Jehovah' 237 times — including Romans 10:13, where 'everyone who calls on the name of the Lord' quotes Joel about YHWH and applies it to *Jesus*. The apostles' inspired practice, not Christendom's conspiracy, is what the manuscripts preserve.

proofs.they: Everlasting life depends on taking in accurate knowledge of Jehovah — which means studying with Jehovah's organization.
proofs.you: The Greek verb ginōskō means to *know someone personally*, not to absorb information — which is why the Watchtower's own 2013 revision quietly changed it to 'their coming to know you.' For six decades the old rendering turned eternal life into a curriculum; the correction concedes the point: eternal life is a relationship, not a study program. Jesus says in the same Gospel, 'you refuse to come to ME that you may have life' (John 5:39-40).

proofs.they: God's law from Noah onward forbids taking blood into the body; transfusion is a modern way of consuming blood.
proofs.you: The decree addresses eating blood — the issue in Genesis 9 and Leviticus 17 and the flashpoint of Jewish-Gentile table fellowship, the actual context of Acts 15. A transfusion no more 'eats' blood than a heart transplant eats a heart; blood transfused stays blood and functions as an organ. Their own position concedes incoherence: since June 2000, fractions of *every* blood component — hemoglobin included — are permitted as conscience matters. And Jesus' rule for ceremonial law versus human life is explicit: 'the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.'

proofs.they: The tree dream's 'seven times' prophetically equals 2,520 years from Jerusalem's fall in 607 BCE, ending in October 1914 when Christ was enthroned in heaven.
proofs.you: Daniel 4 interprets itself: 'it is you, O king' (v.22) — Nebuchadnezzar's seven times of madness, fulfilled in his own lifetime (v.34-37), with no hint of a second fulfillment. The calculation needs five unstated moves: seven 'times' become 360-day years (2,520 days); a day-for-a-year rule imported from unrelated passages turns them into 2,520 years; the start date is set at 607 BCE, which every Babylonian chronology source (business tablets, the astronomical diary VAT 4956) and every historian contradicts — Jerusalem fell in 587/586; and the endpoint is an invisible event no one could verify. Tellingly, Russell inherited this same math from Nelson Barbour and preached 1914 as the END of earthly governments — when that failed, the date was kept and its meaning replaced.
refs: Acts 1:6-7 — 'not for you to know times'

didyouknow.t: 1914 was originally the END of the world, not the beginning of the end
didyouknow.d: Russell taught that Armageddon would be OVER by 1914: 'the battle of the great day of God Almighty... will end in A.D. 1914 with the complete overthrow of earth's present rulership.' When 1914 brought a world war instead of the world's end, the date was recycled as Christ's invisible heavenly enthronement — the failure became the proof.
didyouknow.src: C.T. Russell, The Time Is at Hand (1889)

didyouknow.t: The Watchtower built a San Diego mansion for Abraham and King David
didyouknow.d: Beth Sarim ('House of the Princes'), built 1929, was deeded in perpetual trust for the resurrected 'princes' — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David — expected imminently. Watch Tower president Rutherford lived and wintered there until his death in 1942. The patriarchs never arrived; the Society quietly sold the house in 1948.
didyouknow.src: San Diego deed (1930); Wikipedia, 'Beth Sarim'

didyouknow.t: 'Millions Now Living Will Never Die' — the 1925 prediction
didyouknow.d: Rutherford's 1920 book declared 1925 'definitely settled by the Scriptures' for the return of the faithful patriarchs and the beginning of restoration. 1925 passed; Rutherford later admitted to Bethel staff he had 'made an ass of himself' over it. Many who sold homes and businesses were not reimbursed.
didyouknow.src: J.F. Rutherford, Millions Now Living Will Never Die (1920)

didyouknow.t: The Great Pyramid of Giza was 'God's stone witness' — until it became Satan's
didyouknow.d: For decades the Society taught the Great Pyramid's internal passages, measured in 'pyramid inches,' confirmed 1874 and 1914 chronology — Russell called it God's 'stone witness and prophet.' In 1928 Rutherford reversed course, declaring pyramid study inspired by Satan. A pyramid monument the Society erected still stands at its burial plot near Russell's grave in Pittsburgh (he's under a conventional marker beside it, contrary to folklore).
didyouknow.src: Thy Kingdom Come (1891); Watchtower Nov 15 & Dec 1, 1928

didyouknow.t: The Photo-Drama of Creation was a 1914 multimedia blockbuster
didyouknow.d: An eight-hour presentation of slides and film synchronized with phonograph sound — genuinely pioneering cinema — shown free to audiences totaling around nine million in its first year. It taught, among other things, that 1914 marked the close of the Gentile Times and the imminent end of the present order.
didyouknow.src: Watch Tower Society, Photo-Drama of Creation (1914)

didyouknow.t: The 'Miracle Wheat' scandal
didyouknow.d: In 1911 the Watch Tower sold 'Miracle Wheat' seed at $1 per pound (roughly $30 today), claiming extraordinary yields. When the Brooklyn Daily Eagle mocked the scheme, Russell sued for $100,000 in libel — and lost, after government testing showed the wheat was ordinary. The court record remains public.
didyouknow.src: Russell v. Brooklyn Daily Eagle (1913-1915)

didyouknow.t: 'Judge' Rutherford ran the Society like a corporation and lived like an executive
didyouknow.d: Joseph Rutherford — 'the Judge,' from a brief stint as a substitute judge — centralized all doctrinal authority, replaced elected elders with appointees, and directed the movement from Beth Sarim, driven in 16-cylinder luxury cars during the Great Depression while publishers went door to door unpaid.
didyouknow.src: Wikipedia, 'Joseph Franklin Rutherford'; Penton, Apocalypse Delayed

didyouknow.t: Eight Watch Tower leaders went to prison in 1918
didyouknow.d: Rutherford and seven associates were convicted under the Espionage Act over anti-war passages in 'The Finished Mystery' and sentenced to 20 years; they served about nine months in Atlanta before release on bail in 1919, and the convictions were vacated. The organization now dates Jesus' selection of it as his 'faithful and discreet slave' to precisely 1919 — the year the leaders got out.
didyouknow.src: Wikipedia, 'Joseph Franklin Rutherford'; JW.org's own 1918 centennial article

didyouknow.t: Awake! carried a promise to the 1914 generation on its masthead — then quietly deleted it
didyouknow.d: Until October 22, 1995, every issue's masthead promised 'the Creator's promise of a peaceful and secure new world BEFORE THE GENERATION THAT SAW THE EVENTS OF 1914 PASSES AWAY.' The November 8, 1995 issue dropped the clause without announcement, in step with that month's Watchtower redefining 'this generation.'
didyouknow.src: Awake! Oct 22 vs Nov 8, 1995 mastheads

didyouknow.t: 1975 was heavily promoted as the end of 6,000 years of human history
didyouknow.d: The 1966 book 'Life Everlasting in Freedom of the Sons of God' tied 1975 to the close of six millennia since Adam; articles like 'Why Are You Looking Forward to 1975?' (Watchtower, Aug 15, 1968) stoked expectation, and some sold homes and postponed careers. After the failure, publisher numbers fell for years; a 1980 Watchtower conceded the organization shared blame — while disciplining members who said so.
didyouknow.src: Life Everlasting (1966); Watchtower Aug 15, 1968; Mar 15, 1980

didyouknow.t: 'This generation' now means two overlapping lifespans
didyouknow.d: After redefinitions in 1995 and 2008, the April 15, 2010 Watchtower unveiled the 'overlapping generations' doctrine: the 'generation' of Matthew 24:34 spans anointed ones alive in 1914 PLUS anyone anointed while any of them still lived — anchored publicly on Fred Franz (d. 1992). One verse's 'generation' now stretches toward 130+ years.
didyouknow.src: Watchtower Apr 15, 2010; D. Splane, JW Broadcasting (2015)

didyouknow.t: Memorial partakers are multiplying when they should be vanishing
didyouknow.d: Doctrine says the anointed 'remnant' of the 144,000 (sealed mostly before 1935 in older teaching) should be dying off. Instead, partakers bottomed out around 8,500 in the mid-2000s and have nearly tripled since — the organization's own 2025 report counts 24,576 partakers worldwide (23,212 in 2024).
didyouknow.src: JW.org Service Year Reports, Grand Totals 2024-2025

didyouknow.t: The Watchtower was a UN-associated NGO for nine years
didyouknow.d: While teaching that the United Nations is the scarlet 'wild beast' of Revelation and the 'disgusting thing,' the Watchtower Society held associate NGO status with the UN Department of Public Information from 1992 to 2001 — annually renewed — and withdrew only days after The Guardian exposed it on October 8, 2001.
didyouknow.src: The Guardian, Oct 8, 2001; UN DPI letter

didyouknow.t: Organ transplants: cannibalism in 1967, conscience matter in 1980
didyouknow.d: The Watchtower of November 15, 1967 classed transplants as 'cannibalism, a practice abhorrent to all civilized people'; Witnesses declined kidneys and corneas accordingly. In 1980 the position reversed to personal conscience. No apology was made to those who lost organs, sight, or life in the interval.
didyouknow.src: Watchtower Nov 15, 1967; Mar 15, 1980

didyouknow.t: The blood ban permits 'fractions' of everything it bans
didyouknow.d: Whole blood and its four 'primary components' are forbidden, but since the June 15, 2000 Watchtower, fractions derived from ANY component are a conscience matter — including hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying core of red cells. A Witness may refuse red cells yet accept bovine-derived hemoglobin. No principled line explains where a 'component' ends and a 'fraction' begins.
didyouknow.src: Watchtower June 15, 2000; AJWRB

didyouknow.t: Awake! celebrated 26 children who died refusing blood
didyouknow.d: The May 22, 1994 Awake! cover — 'Youths Who Put God First' — displayed photos of 26 young Witnesses who died refusing transfusions, presented as exemplary. The accompanying text said youths who put God first 'are still doing it, only today the drama is played out in hospitals and courtrooms, with blood transfusions the issue.'
didyouknow.src: Awake! May 22, 1994

didyouknow.t: Every publisher carries a no-blood card
didyouknow.d: Witnesses carry a signed Advance Decision / durable power of attorney document refusing blood transfusion even if unconscious and dying, typically renewed annually and often witnessed by congregation elders — which also means the congregation knows if it isn't signed.
didyouknow.src: JW.org medical information documents

didyouknow.t: Ex-members are officially 'mentally diseased'
didyouknow.d: The July 15, 2011 Watchtower told members: 'apostates are mentally diseased, and they seek to infect others with their disloyal teachings' — quotation marks around a phrase lifted from 1 Timothy 6:4's 'obsessed.' UK police in Portsmouth examined whether the article breached religious-hatred law.
didyouknow.src: Watchtower July 15, 2011, pp. 15-19; The Independent (2011)

didyouknow.t: Australia's Royal Commission: 1,006 alleged abusers, zero reported by the organization
didyouknow.d: The 2015-2016 Royal Commission found JW Australia's own files recorded 1,006 alleged child sexual abusers since 1950 — and the organization itself reported not one to police (383 cases reached police via victims or families). The Commission singled out the two-witness rule's 'inflexible' application to child abuse as a systemic failure. The organization still applies the rule.
didyouknow.src: Royal Commission Case Study 29 (2016)

didyouknow.t: Russia banned Jehovah's Witnesses as 'extremist' in 2017
didyouknow.d: On April 20, 2017 Russia's Supreme Court liquidated the JW administrative center and its 395 local organizations, seizing all property; hundreds of Witnesses have since been prosecuted or imprisoned. The persecution is real and worth condemning without reservation — and internally it is read as prophecy being fulfilled, which strengthens rather than tests conviction.
didyouknow.src: Human Rights Watch, Apr 20, 2017; USCIRF

didyouknow.t: After 103 years, the hour ledger closed — mostly
didyouknow.d: From 1920 to 2023 every publisher filed a monthly report of hours spent preaching. As of November 2023, rank-and-file publishers just check a box for participation — but pioneers and missionaries still count hours, and congregation records still distinguish the 'regular' from the 'irregular' and 'inactive.'
didyouknow.src: 2023 Annual Meeting; Religion News Service, Nov 27, 2023

didyouknow.t: 'Disfellowshipped' was rebranded in 2024 — the shunning wasn't
didyouknow.d: The August 2024 Watchtower retired the word 'disfellowshipped' for 'removed from the congregation,' and now permits a brief greeting at the Kingdom Hall. Members are still directed not to associate with removed ones — including family outside the household. The vocabulary softened; the mechanism survived.
didyouknow.src: Watchtower Aug 2024, study ed.; JW.org FAQ 'removed from the congregation'

didyouknow.t: JW.org is the most-translated website on earth
didyouknow.d: Content in over 1,100 languages including 100+ sign languages — more than Google, Wikipedia, and Apple combined. It's a genuinely staggering translation operation, and it means the same centrally-produced sentences reach every member on the planet simultaneously; there is no local theological variation to compare notes against.
didyouknow.src: Religion News Service, Nov 4, 2019; jw.org

didyouknow.t: Windowless Kingdom Halls: the folklore and the reality
didyouknow.d: The rumor says halls have no windows 'to keep members from escaping.' The reality is duller: many halls are windowless or minimally windowed for construction cost, security, and vandalism reasons, and plenty have ordinary windows. The buildings aren't the cage; the exit costs are.
didyouknow.src: JW regional building design guidelines; site surveys

didyouknow.t: 'No paid clergy' — except the ones with vows
didyouknow.d: Witnesses proudly have no salaried pastorate, and local elders are genuinely unpaid volunteers. But Bethel workers, circuit overseers, and the Governing Body belong to the Worldwide Order of Special Full-Time Servants — housed, fed, insured, and supported by the organization under a vow of poverty. There is a professional religious class; it just isn't called clergy.
didyouknow.src: Watch Tower legal filings; Organized to Do Jehovah's Will

week.t: Midweek meeting: 'Our Christian Life and Ministry'
week.d: About 1¾ hours on a weeknight: Bible-reading assignments, student demonstrations of door-step conversations, and organizational instruction, all from a centrally published workbook identical worldwide.
week.tip: If you visit, notice that student 'talks' rehearse conversations with people like you — your objections have been practiced on stage.

week.t: Weekend meeting: public talk + Watchtower study
week.d: A 30-minute public talk from an approved outline, then an hour studying that week's Watchtower article: a reader reads the paragraph, the conductor asks the printed question, hands go up to restate the paragraph.
week.tip: Answering 'in your own words' means paraphrasing the paragraph — original analysis from the floor is not the exercise. Attend once; it explains everything about how doctrine propagates.

week.d: Door-to-door and return visits, usually organized in car groups after a brief meeting. Since November 2023 most publishers no longer log hours — but participation is still reported monthly and noticed.
week.tip: The person at your door may be as tired as you are. Offering coffee and an unhurried conversation is rarer for them than an argument — and far more destabilizing to the script.

week.d: Two publishers stand by a literature cart in a public spot, trained NOT to approach — passersby must initiate. It counts as witnessing and suits members exhausted by doors.
week.tip: Cart witnesses expect to be ignored. A friendly question — 'what made you personally sure this is the truth?' — is often the first real conversation of their shift.

week.d: One weeknight reserved for parent-led study of Watchtower materials — established in 2009 when the separate congregation book study was folded into the midweek meeting.
week.tip: For JW kids this is a third structured religious evening weekly. Understanding the sheer time-load explains why 'just read this book I like' is a bigger ask than it sounds.

week.d: Every publisher files monthly: now a checkbox for sharing in the ministry plus a count of Bible studies; pioneers still report hours. Miss enough months and you're classed 'irregular,' then 'inactive' — labels elders track.
week.tip: Spiritual health is operationalized as reported activity. When a Witness friend seems anxious near month's end, this is often why.

week.d: Their only holy day: an evening Lord's Supper after sundown corresponding to Nisan 14, with the bread and wine passed hand to hand — and declined by nearly everyone present, since only the 'anointed' may partake. Attendance (about 21 million) triples membership.
week.tip: It's their biggest invitation event and the easiest meeting to attend. Watching a room pass the emblems untasted is the two-class doctrine made visible — worth seeing once, gently discussed after.

week.d: Two one-day circuit assemblies plus a three-day regional convention each year: baptisms, new releases, and dramatizations. Vacation time is expected to bend around them.
week.tip: Conventions are where new doctrine and policy premiere. Asking a friend 'what changed this year?' is a non-hostile way to surface the fact that things do change.

week.d: Alleged 'serious sin' (fornication, apostasy, smoking, celebrating Christmas...) goes before three elders in a closed meeting — no observers, no advocate, no recordings permitted. Outcomes range from reproof to removal from the congregation.
week.tip: If a Witness friend goes quiet and distressed, a committee may be why. Knowing the process exists helps you ask better questions and judge less.

week.d: No birthday parties, no holiday crafts or carols, no standing for the anthem or saluting the flag, no extracurricular sports typically, and often the only Witness in class — a weekly exercise in being conspicuously different.
week.tip: For a JW child, being singled out at school is pre-framed as persecution and proof of faith. Kind, unremarkable inclusion — with a parent-approved alternative in hand — lands better than making an example either way.

week.d: Between pre-studying the Watchtower article, the midweek workbook, assigned Bible chapters, and family worship, a conscientious publisher's week holds four to six timetabled spiritual obligations before any field service.
week.tip: 'Come to church Sunday AND a midweek thing AND read this' mirrors the structure they're exhausted by. One unhurried meal with no agenda is the counter-cultural move.

aboutyou.t: You are 'Christendom' — and Christendom is Babylon the Great
aboutyou.d: All non-JW Christianity is classed as part of 'Babylon the Great, the world empire of false religion,' whose destruction opens Armageddon. Your baptism, your communion, your prayers are not misguided worship in their eyes — they are false religion awaiting judgment.
aboutyou.tip: Don't spend energy proving your denomination is nice. The category itself is the claim to examine: ask where Scripture teaches that everyone outside one 1919-appointed organization is Babylon.

aboutyou.t: Your church is scheduled for destruction
aboutyou.d: They expect governments, turning on religion, to destroy the churches as the tribulation begins — an event they anticipate rather than mourn. Loving individuals may genuinely hope you'll 'get out of her' before then.
aboutyou.tip: Hear the affection inside the warning: door-knocking at your house is, in their frame, pulling you from a burning building. Respond to the love, then question the fire.

aboutyou.t: Your cross is a pagan idol
aboutyou.d: They teach Jesus died on an upright 'torture stake' and that the cross is a pagan symbol Christians should not display or wear. A crucifix on your wall reads to them roughly as an idol.
aboutyou.tip: Skip the archaeology duel first; ask the value question — **why would the shape of the instrument matter more than the death upon it?** (1 Corinthians 1:18 glories in the cross, whatever its geometry.)

aboutyou.t: The Trinity is, to them, a satanic deception
aboutyou.d: Watchtower literature has long traced the Trinity to Babylonian and pagan triads and presented it as Satan's masterstroke of misdirection. When you say 'God the Son,' they hear the signature lie of false religion.
aboutyou.tip: Definitions first: most JWs rebut tritheism ('three gods') because that's what they were taught the Trinity is. Establish 'one God in three persons — not three gods, not one person in costume' before any verse is worth exchanging.

aboutyou.t: Your ex-JW friend is the most dangerous person you know
aboutyou.d: 'Apostates' — especially former members — are described as 'mentally diseased' (Watchtower, July 15, 2011), and members are trained to refuse all contact with them and their words. Citing an ex-JW source can end a conversation instantly.
aboutyou.tip: Never open with 'I talked to an ex-Witness.' Use their own publications and the Bible — sources they're allowed to look at — and save survivor testimony for when trust is deep.

aboutyou.t: They can't take your literature — or your holiday greetings
aboutyou.d: Non-JW religious material is off-limits ('apostate' material especially — framed like spiritual poison), and 'Merry Christmas' obliges an awkward decline. The refusal is trained, not personal.
aboutyou.tip: Don't hand them a book; ask a question they'll carry home. Questions get through customs; pamphlets don't.

aboutyou.d: They are catechized to expect opposition as proof of being the true faith — Russia's 2017 ban is taught as prophecy fulfilled. Hostility, mockery, and doorstep debate all land as 'we were told this would happen.'
aboutyou.tip: This is why gentleness IS the argument. The one experience the persecution-frame cannot metabolize is a warm, unhurried Christian who asks good questions and doesn't slam the door.

aboutyou.t: You're being measured by how you treat THEM
aboutyou.d: Their reading of the sheep and the goats (Matthew 25) says the nations are judged by their response to Christ's anointed 'brothers' — i.e., to the Witnesses and their message. Your reception at the door is, doctrinally, your judgment scene in miniature.
aboutyou.tip: Use the frame kindly: receive them as you would Christ's own — food, respect, patience — and then ask who Matthew 25 actually calls 'the least of these,' and whether verse 46's outcome ('everlasting punishment') fits annihilation.

aboutyou.d: Interfaith activity — praying with you, attending your service (except perhaps a funeral or wedding, silently), joining a Bible study you lead — is forbidden as false worship. Declining your prayer isn't coldness; it's compliance.
aboutyou.tip: Offer instead of insisting: 'May I pray for you — right now, out loud? You don't have to join, just listen.' Listening isn't participating, and almost no one refuses being prayed FOR.

aboutyou.t: You are 'worldly,' and friendship with you is a managed risk
aboutyou.d: Everything outside the organization is 'the world' lying in Satan's power (their reading of 1 John 5:19); 'bad associations spoil useful habits' (1 Corinthians 15:33) is applied to close friendship with you. Real warmth is possible, but deep unsupervised friendship draws counsel.
aboutyou.tip: Expect a ceiling on the relationship and don't take it personally. Consistent, undemanding kindness over years is exactly the data point the 'worldly people are Satan's' doctrine can't explain.

doctrine.theirs: Jehovah is the one almighty God, a single divine person, and his personal name matters supremely. The Trinity is a pagan-influenced doctrine adopted centuries after Christ, unreasonable and unscriptural — Jesus is God's Son, never 'God the Son.' Honoring Jehovah means rejecting the Trinity as a teaching that dishonors him.
doctrine.bible: There is one God (Deuteronomy 6:4) — and the Father is called God (John 6:27), the Son is called God (John 1:1; 20:28; Hebrews 1:8), the Spirit is God (Acts 5:3-4), yet they are distinct persons who speak to and about one another. Jesus receives worship (Matthew 28:9,17; Hebrews 1:6), forgives sins (Mark 2:5-7), and shares the Father's glory 'before the world was' (John 17:5). Baptism is into one name — of the Father AND the Son AND the holy spirit (Matthew 28:19).
doctrine.key: The question is not whether the word 'Trinity' appears, but whether the Bible presents one God existing as Father, Son, and Spirit — and it does on every page of the New Testament.

doctrine.theirs: Jesus is God's first creation, the archangel Michael, who was used to create everything else. He lived a perfect human life as a ransom, was raised as a mighty spirit creature, and has ruled invisibly as heavenly King since 1914. He is 'a god' (John 1:1 NWT) — divine-like, but not Jehovah.
doctrine.bible: Hebrews 1 exists to deny exactly this: 'to which of the angels did God ever say, You are my Son?' (1:5), 'let all God's angels worship him' (1:6), and the Son is addressed as 'God' whose throne is forever (1:8). Michael 'did not dare' rebuke Satan (Jude 9); Jesus rebuked him freely (Matthew 4:10). No verse states Jesus is Michael — the identification is inferred from a trumpet-and-voice text (1 Thessalonians 4:16).
doctrine.key: If the whole point of Hebrews 1 is that the Son is categorically above every angel, the Son cannot be an angel.

doctrine.theirs: The holy spirit is not a person but Jehovah's active force — the invisible power he sends forth to accomplish his will, comparable to a hand or to electricity. It is therefore written lowercase and is not to be worshipped or prayed to.
doctrine.bible: The Spirit speaks (Acts 13:2), teaches and reminds (John 14:26), can be lied to — and lying to him is lying to God (Acts 5:3-4) — can be grieved (Ephesians 4:30), intercedes (Romans 8:26-27), and distributes gifts 'just as he wills' (1 Corinthians 12:11). Forces don't will, grieve, or say 'me' (Acts 13:2).
doctrine.key: Every personal capacity — will, speech, knowledge, grief — is ascribed to the Spirit; 'active force' requires explaining all of them away.

doctrine.theirs: Exactly 144,000 'anointed' Christians are born again, taken into the new covenant, and will rule with Christ in heaven. The 'great crowd' — virtually all Witnesses today — hope to survive Armageddon and live forever on a paradise earth, gaining final salvation after faithfulness through Christ's thousand-year reign and a final test. Only the anointed partake of the Memorial emblems.
doctrine.bible: 'Unless someone is born again he cannot SEE the kingdom of God' (John 3:3) — stated to Nicodemus with no ceiling of 144,000. 'Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves' (John 6:53). There is 'one body and one spirit... one hope' (Ephesians 4:4), and salvation is by grace through faith, not survival plus a millennium of works (Ephesians 2:8-9; Romans 8:1).
doctrine.key: The New Testament knows one flock, one hope, and one table — a salvation system that tells 99.7% of its members not to touch the bread and wine has no apostolic precedent.

doctrine.theirs: The soul is the person, not something a person has; when you die, you cease to exist entirely. 'The dead are conscious of nothing at all' (Ecclesiastes 9:5). The hope is not survival of death but future re-creation by resurrection — God remembers you perfectly and remakes you.
doctrine.bible: Jesus: 'today you will be with me in Paradise' (Luke 23:43 — the NWT relocates the comma). Paul desires 'to depart and be with Christ, which is far better' (Philippians 1:23) and calls being absent from the body being 'at home with the Lord' (2 Corinthians 5:8). Jesus warns of the One who can destroy 'both soul and body' — two things, not one (Matthew 10:28); Moses and Elijah appear conversing at the Transfiguration.
doctrine.key: If death is nonexistence, departing to be with Christ cannot be 'far better' — there would be no one there to be with him.

doctrine.theirs: Hell (Sheol/Hades) is simply the common grave of mankind; hellfire is a slander on God's love. The unredeemed wicked are annihilated — punished with everlasting destruction in the sense of permanent nonexistence — most at Armageddon, with no conscious afterlife of any kind.
doctrine.bible: Jesus speaks of judgment more soberly than anyone: 'everlasting punishment' set in parallel with 'everlasting life' (Matthew 25:46 — the same adjective governing both), the rich man conscious in Hades (Luke 16:23-24), and torment 'day and night forever' for the devil, beast, and false prophet (Revelation 20:10) in the lake into which the condemned also go (20:15). Christians debate the nature of final punishment honestly; Scripture does not permit reducing it to painless deletion at Armageddon based on chronology.
doctrine.key: Whatever hell's precise nature, Matthew 25:46 will not allow 'everlasting' to mean eternal for life but momentary for punishment.

doctrine.theirs: Jesus was raised a spirit creature; his physical body was not raised — God removed or dissolved it. His post-resurrection appearances were materialized bodies assumed for the occasion, which is why he wasn't always recognized. He returned, invisibly, as a spirit king in 1914.
doctrine.bible: Jesus staked the claim in advance: 'destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up... he was talking about the temple of his body' (John 2:19-21). Risen, he insists 'a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have' (Luke 24:39), eats fish, and invites Thomas's fingers into the wounds — the same body, glorified. The tomb was empty because the body that died is the body that rose (1 Corinthians 15).
doctrine.key: A 'resurrection' that leaves the corpse dissolved is precisely what Jesus said would NOT happen to the temple of his body.

doctrine.theirs: The 'seven times' of Daniel 4 equal 2,520 years running from Jerusalem's destruction in 607 BCE to October 1914, when Christ was enthroned in heaven and Satan was cast down to earth. World War I, quakes, famines, and the preaching work prove we've been in the last days since; 'this generation' — now two overlapping groups of anointed ones — will see the end.
doctrine.bible: Daniel 4 announces its own meaning: 'it is you, O king' — fulfilled in Nebuchadnezzar's madness within his own reign, with no second application offered anywhere in Scripture. Jesus forbade exactly this arithmetic: 'it does not belong to you to know the times or seasons' (Acts 1:7); 'nobody knows that day or hour' (Matthew 24:36); and he pre-refuted invisible comings — 'if they say he is in the inner rooms, do not believe it... as lightning flashes, so the Son of man will be' (Matthew 24:26-27).
doctrine.key: 607 BCE is contradicted by all historical evidence (Jerusalem fell 587/586), and without 607 there is no 1914 — the organization's entire claim to authority stands on a date only it defends.

doctrine.topic: The organization and the faithful slave
doctrine.theirs: Jehovah has always worked through a visible channel; today that channel is the 'faithful and discreet slave' — the Governing Body — appointed by Christ over his belongings in 1919 to dispense spiritual food at the proper time. Loyalty to Jehovah is inseparable from loyalty to his organization; salvation requires coming to it. Jesus is mediator of the new covenant for the anointed 144,000, not for the great crowd directly.
doctrine.bible: 'There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, a man, Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom FOR ALL' (1 Timothy 2:5-6). The 'faithful and discreet slave' is a character in a parable about watchfulness (Matthew 24:45-51), not a prophecy of a 1919 corporate appointment — and the same parable warns that the slave may prove wicked. The Beroeans were commended for verifying an apostle against Scripture (Acts 17:11); no organization is above that test.
doctrine.key: Any system in which Christ's mediation reaches you only through a committee has replaced the one Mediator with many.

doctrine.theirs: Blood is sacred, representing life, and God's law from Noah through Acts 15 forbids taking it into the body — including by transfusion. Whole blood and its four primary components (red cells, white cells, platelets, plasma) must be refused even at the cost of life; fractions derived from any component are a personal conscience matter, as are non-blood alternatives.
doctrine.bible: Every biblical blood text concerns eating blood or its ritual use (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:10-12; Acts 15:28-29 in a table-fellowship context) — and the law itself made life-saving exceptions, as Jesus argued: David ate forbidden showbread and was guiltless; 'the Sabbath was made for man' (Mark 2:25-27); 'I want mercy, and not sacrifice' (Matthew 12:7). The command's stated logic — blood poured out because life belongs to God — is honored, not violated, by using blood to save a life.
doctrine.key: A rule that forbids red cells but permits hemoglobin, and that has cost children's lives (Awake!, May 22, 1994), is not the weightier matters of the law — justice, mercy, faithfulness.

doctrine.theirs: God's original purpose for a paradise earth will be fulfilled: after Armageddon, the great crowd will transform the globe into a garden during Christ's thousand-year reign, the dead will be resurrected to earth, and obedient mankind will live forever here in perfection. Heaven is for the 144,000 only; earth is not destined for destruction but for restoration.
doctrine.bible: The renewed earth is a genuinely biblical hope Christians share — 'the meek will inherit the earth' (Matthew 5:5); creation itself will be set free (Romans 8:21); 'new heavens and a new earth' (2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:1). But Scripture never splits redeemed humanity into permanent heaven-people and earth-people: the New Jerusalem comes DOWN, God dwells with mankind, and the throne is on the renewed earth for all his servants, who 'will see his face' (Revelation 21:2-3; 22:3-4).
doctrine.key: The Bible's ending is not two eternal address lists but one — heaven and earth reunited, with every redeemed person in God's immediate presence.

doctrine.theirs: True worship excludes anything with pagan roots or nationalistic meaning: no Christmas, Easter, birthdays, or holidays; no flag salute, anthems, voting, or military service; no cross imagery. Worship centers on meeting attendance, public preaching, personal study of the organization's publications, and using God's name Jehovah. Political neutrality and moral cleanness mark God's people.
doctrine.bible: Conscientious neutrality and moral seriousness deserve respect — but the apostles handled disputable days differently: 'one man judges one day as above another; another judges all days alike; let each be fully convinced in his own mind' (Romans 14:5), and 'let no one judge you... in respect of a festival' (Colossians 2:16). Where Scripture leaves freedom, binding every member's conscience organization-wide — on penalty of judicial action — is what Jesus rebuked in the Pharisees (Mark 7:7-9).
doctrine.key: The issue isn't whether a Christian may skip Christmas — of course they may — but whether anyone may be shunned for keeping it: 'why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?' (1 Corinthians 10:29).

nwt-translation.t: The New World Translation is the most accurate Bible available — it restored God's name and freed the text from Christendom's bias. John 1:1 correctly reads 'the Word was a god.'

I love that you take translation seriously — most people never check. Help me with one thing: **who translated it?** Every other major Bible publishes its committee's names and credentials so scholars can be examined.
The translators chose to remain anonymous so the glory goes to Jehovah, not to men.

That's a beautiful motive — but it also means no one can verify their Greek and Hebrew. The one member later identified, Frederick Franz, had no degree in biblical languages. And on 'a god': the same Greek construction appears in John 1:6, 1:12, 1:18 — the NWT translates it 'God' there. **Why does theos become 'a god' only in the one verse where it describes Jesus?**
The Governing Body has scholars who reviewed all of this. Jehovah's organization wouldn't give us an inaccurate Bible — we trust the channel Jehovah is using.

And I hear that trust — it's sincere. But notice what just happened: the answer to a Greek grammar question was 'trust the organization.' The Beroeans were praised for checking even the apostle Paul against Scripture. **If the translation can only be defended by trusting its publisher, how would you ever find out if it were wrong?** I'd genuinely love to read John 1 with you in any translation you pick — even an interlinear from your own Kingdom Hall library.

chronology-607.t: Bible chronology proves Jerusalem was destroyed in 607 BCE, and counting the 'seven times' of Daniel 4 — 2,520 years — brings you exactly to October 1914, when Christ began ruling as King.

You clearly know this material better than most — can I ask about just the starting point? Every reference work, every Babylonian business tablet, and astronomical diaries like VAT 4956 date Jerusalem's fall to 587 or 586 BCE. **Do you know of any historian or archaeologist outside the organization who defends 607?**
Secular historians rely on pagan records that can be wrong. We start from the Bible: Jerusalem lay desolate seventy years, and Babylon fell in 539 — count back and you get 607.

That's fair reasoning, so let's use only the Bible: Jeremiah 25:11-12 says the seventy years are nations serving the KING OF BABYLON, ended by Babylon's fall in 539 — servitude, not desolation, which fits 605-539. And Zechariah 1:12, written around 519, speaks of seventy years still being lamented — decades after your count ends. But here's my real question: **if 607 moves by even twenty years, what happens to 1914?**
1914 is confirmed by world events — war, earthquakes, the sign of the last days. The faithful slave has helped us understand the chronology, and the events prove they were right.

Yet the organization itself was appointed — by its own teaching — in 1919 BECAUSE 1914 was true. The date proves the organization and the organization vouches for the date; that circle is worth sitting with. I say this as a friend, not a prosecutor: **you deserve a foundation that survives checking.** Would you be willing to look at the seventy-years verses with me sometime, just the two of us and the text?

failed-dates.t: Jehovah's people have always been eager for the end — sometimes expectations ran ahead of the light. But Proverbs 4:18 says the light gets brighter, and our understanding has been refined.

I appreciate the honesty in that — everyone's tradition has embarrassments, mine included. But can we look at the specifics together? 1914 was preached as the end of all earthly governments; 1925 was 'definitely settled by the Scriptures' for Abraham's return — there was a mansion waiting; 1975 emptied savings accounts. **These weren't private guesses — they were published worldwide as Scripture's own timetable.**
Even the apostles expected the Kingdom in their day. Being wrong about timing out of eagerness isn't the same as being a false prophet.

The apostles asked and Jesus said it wasn't theirs to know — and after Pentecost they never once published a date. Here's the test I can't get around: Deuteronomy 18:22 says when a word spoken in Jehovah's name does not come true, don't fear it. The Watchtower called itself Jehovah's channel while announcing those dates. **Does 'brighter light' explain saying false things in Jehovah's name — or does it just rename them?**
The organization has admitted mistakes were made. What matters is that Jehovah kept using them — look at the worldwide preaching work. No one else is doing that.

Notice, though — when the dates failed, members who said so were disfellowshipped, while the leaders who published them kept their seats. That asymmetry troubles me for your sake, not against you. **If a hundred years of dated predictions all failed, what future claim from the same source could ever be tested?** You're allowed to love God and still ask that. I'll ask it with you anytime, over coffee, no scorekeeping.

prophecy-authority.t: Jesus said the faithful and discreet slave would give food at the proper time. In 1919 he inspected all who claimed to serve God and appointed the anointed brothers taking the lead — today the Governing Body — over all his belongings.

That's the load-bearing wall of everything else, isn't it — so it's worth weighing carefully. Just historically: **what was Christ inspecting in 1919 that he approved?** In 1919 the Society was still teaching that the Great Pyramid was God's stone witness, that the last days began in 1799, and that Christ returned in 1874. All of that was later discarded as error — some of it as satanic.
They had some wrong expectations, but their hearts were clean and they were preaching the Kingdom. Jehovah looks at the heart.

Amen — he does, and I don't doubt those hearts. But the claim isn't 'sincere people'; it's a legal appointment as the sole channel of truth, dated to a year when nearly everything they taught was, by the current Governing Body's own standard, false. And Matthew 24 is a parable urging EVERY servant to stay faithful — verse 48 warns the same slave could prove wicked. **Where in the text is a 1919 appointment of a corporation — and who verified it besides the corporation?**

Someone has to take the lead. Jehovah has always used an organization — Israel, then the first-century governing body in Jerusalem. Without the slave we'd have confusion, like Christendom's thousands of sects.

Order matters, agreed — but Acts 15 shows apostles and elders reasoning from Scripture in the open, and Paul telling churches to test even angels and apostles against the gospel (Galatians 1:8, Acts 17:11). Unity purchased by forbidding examination isn't the unity of the Spirit; it's the silence of the room. Gently: **if the appointment claim is true, it can survive your investigation — so what would it cost you to investigate it?** I'm safe company for that question, whenever you want.

doctrine-of-god.t: We worship Jehovah, the only true God. Jesus is his Son — the first creation — and never claimed to be God. The Trinity confuses people and dishonors the Father.

Can I say first — your reverence for God's honor is something I genuinely respect. Let me ask about one scene: risen Jesus stands before Thomas, who says 'My Lord and my GOD' (John 20:28). Jesus doesn't correct him — he blesses those who believe the same without seeing. **If Jesus were not God, wasn't that the moment to say so?**
Thomas was exclaiming in astonishment — or acknowledging Jesus as 'a god,' a divine one, like the NWT says at John 1:1. Jesus himself said the Father is greater than he is.

An exclamation using God's title as a swear-word would be blasphemy on the spot — and John wrote the verse as the Gospel's climax: 'these were written that you may believe.' As for 'greater' — the sent one submits to the sender (a king is greater than the prince on campaign) without being a different kind of being; that's Philippians 2, equality laid aside for the mission. Here's my honest question: **Isaiah 44:24 says Jehovah stretched out the heavens ALONE — 'who was with me?' — yet John 1:3 says nothing was created without the Word. How can both be true unless the Word is Jehovah's own being?**

Jehovah created Jesus first and then used him for everything else — that's what 'firstborn of all creation' means. The organization has explained these deep things; we can't lean on our own understanding.

Notice the NWT itself had to add 'other' to Colossians 1 — 'all OTHER things' — to keep Jesus inside creation; the Greek just says all things, through him and FOR him. Friend, I'm not asking you to lean on your understanding or mine, but on the text in front of us both. **Would you read Hebrews 1 aloud with me — just that one chapter — and tell me honestly whether its author thought the Son was an angel?** No trap; I'll bring the NWT.

two-class-salvation.t: The Bible speaks of two hopes: 144,000 anointed ones who rule with Christ in heaven, and the great crowd who live forever on paradise earth. We know we're the great crowd — the heavenly calling was mostly sealed long ago.

Here's what moves me about that, honestly: it decides in advance what Scripture's promises are allowed to mean for YOU. So one gentle question first — at the Last Supper, Jesus said 'this is my blood of the covenant.' At your Memorial, the bread and wine pass down the row and almost no one partakes. **Jesus said 'unless you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves' (John 6:53) — who told you that wasn't addressed to you?**

The emblems are for those in the new covenant — the anointed with the heavenly hope. The great crowd benefits from the ransom without being party to the covenant. The faithful slave has made the two classes clear from Revelation 7 and 14.

But look at Revelation 7 with fresh eyes: the 144,000 are sealed from twelve named tribes of Israel — with Dan missing — and in chapter 14 they're male celibates. Everyone agrees those details are symbolic; only the number is kept literal. Meanwhile the great crowd is 'before the throne... in his temple' — and Revelation 19:1 puts a great crowd IN HEAVEN. **If the tribes, the maleness, and the virginity are symbols, on what basis is 144,000 arithmetic?**

Numbers in Revelation can be literal when the context shows it. Anyway, I don't feel the heavenly calling — I love the thought of paradise earth, seeing resurrected loved ones, petting lions. That's the hope Jehovah's organization has always shown us from Scripture.

And a renewed earth IS in Scripture — we agree there, truly; Revelation ends with heaven coming down to earth, God's tent with mankind, every servant seeing his face (21:3, 22:4). What Scripture never does is post some believers at a distance forever. That promise — seeing HIS face — is written to all who are his. **Would you take the emblems question home this year — read John 6 and Luke 22 before the Memorial, and ask Jehovah directly whether Jesus meant you?** That prayer can't be wrong to pray.

blood-doctrine.t: Blood is sacred to Jehovah — it represents life itself. From Noah to the apostolic decree, 'abstain from blood' is unambiguous. We carry no-blood cards because obeying God matters more than extending life a few years.

I want to honor what's real here: that's costly obedience, and I don't laugh at it. But let me ask about the boundary itself. Acts 15 concerns eating blood — the issue since Genesis 9 was consuming a creature's life. A transfusion doesn't feed anyone; the blood keeps doing its job as living tissue, like a transplanted kidney. **If a doctor said 'abstain from alcohol,' would that forbid rubbing alcohol on a wound?**
Taking it into your veins is still taking it into your body. The organization has explained that the principle covers transfusion — and Jehovah blessed us with bloodless medicine as a result.

Bloodless surgery advances are genuinely good fruit — granted gladly. But here's what I can't resolve: the policy forbids red cells yet permits hemoglobin — which is most of the red cell — plus fractions of every 'forbidden' component, each as a conscience matter since 2000. **If blood is too sacred to transfuse, how can nearly all of it, piece by piece, be fine?** A line that moves like that looks like policy, not principle.

The faithful slave refines our understanding as knowledge increases. Where the Bible doesn't give details, conscience decides — but the clear command stands, and I trust Jehovah more than I fear death.

Your courage isn't in question — only the command's address. When David's men were starving, they ate the holy showbread, and Jesus defended it: 'the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath'; 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' Blood was poured out precisely because life belongs to God — using it to SAVE a life honors that logic. **May I ask just one thing of you — not to change your card tonight, but to read Mark 2:23-27 asking whether Jesus would sign it?** And know this: if you were ever in that hospital bed, I'd be beside you either way.

shunning-exit.t: We don't shun anyone. People are free to leave — and removal from the congregation is loving discipline that protects the flock and often moves the person to come back to Jehovah.

I believe you've seen it work that way for some, and I know the intent is love. But can we be concrete? If your grown daughter concluded — honestly, prayerfully — that the Governing Body isn't God's channel, and said so, she'd face a judicial committee and removal. Then you'd be directed not to associate with her. **Is that freedom to leave, or freedom to leave everyone you love behind?**

That's painful, but it's Scriptural — 'remove the wicked man from among yourselves,' 'do not receive him into your homes.' And the door is always open; the shunning is meant to help them miss Jehovah and return.

Those verses address unrepentant immorality and men actively deceiving churches — Paul never cuts off a doubter; Jude says 'show mercy to those who doubt.' Notice, too, whom the policy actually pressures: not the convinced apostate, but the quiet questioner who now knows the price of honesty. **What does it do to a family's love when everyone knows it can be switched off by committee?** Even the August 2024 adjustment — a greeting allowed at the Kingdom Hall — concedes the old line wasn't Scripture but policy, changeable by print run.
The Governing Body adjusts things as Jehovah directs. I trust that. Without loyalty to the organization there'd be no clean congregation at all.

Here's the thought I'd leave with you, offered gently because I'm not going anywhere: a message that's true doesn't need exit costs; the truth keeps people by being true. Jesus asked the Twelve 'do you want to go also?' with the door wide open — and they stayed for HIM. **If the teaching is solid, why must leaving cost your mother?** Whatever you ever decide, my table doesn't have a committee. That's not rhetoric; it's an invitation.

institutional.t: Jehovah's organization is the cleanest people on earth — no war-blessing, no political entanglement, no scandal-ridden clergy like Christendom's churches.

Churches have real sins on the books — I won't defend a single one of them. But held to its own standard: the Watchtower Society was an associate NGO of the United Nations from 1992 to 2001 — the very organization it calls the wild beast — and withdrew only after The Guardian exposed it. **If a Witness had privately affiliated with the UN for nine years, what would a judicial committee have done?**
That's an apostate distortion. I've heard the association was only for access to the UN library, and it required no membership commitment.

Check it against sources you'd accept in any other case — the UN's own letter states associate NGOs were required to support the UN's ideals and renew annually, which the Society did nine times. And there's harder ground: Australia's Royal Commission examined the organization's OWN files — 1,006 alleged child abusers since 1950, not one reported to authorities by the organization, largely due to the two-witness rule. **Shouldn't 'by their fruits you will recognize them' apply to every tree, including this one?**
Imperfect men have always been part of Jehovah's arrangement — look at Israel's kings. The organization isn't inspired, but it's still the channel Jehovah is using. Where else would we go?

Friend, notice that 'imperfect men' now covers what 'Babylon the Great' condemns in everyone else — that's two scales, and Proverbs calls that detestable. And that last question — Peter's actual words weren't 'where else would we go' but '**Lord, to WHOM shall we go?**' (John 6:68). A person, not a headquarters. That question deserves your best years, and you can explore it without me ever gloating — that's a promise.

practice.t: Christmas, Easter, birthdays — all pagan in origin. December 25 was a sun festival; the only birthday parties in the Bible ended with executions. True worship must be clean of Babylonish customs.

You're right about more of the history than most Christians know, honestly — December 25 isn't in the Bible and nobody's required to keep it. But test the rule itself: your literature acknowledges wedding rings likely have pagan roots, yet allows them because of what they mean NOW. **Why does 'present meaning matters' rescue the ring but not a child's birthday cake?**

The Bible mentions wedding rings neutrally — but it records both birthday feasts negatively, Pharaoh's and Herod's. And the organization has shown these celebrations promote creature worship and greed.

Two wicked kings threw parties and did wicked things AT them — Scripture never says the anniversary was the sin; both texts condemn the killings, not the cake. And Job's children held feasts 'each on his own day' while Job stays blameless. The apostles faced this exact question about days and food offered to idols, and their answer was liberty: 'let each be fully convinced in his own mind' (Romans 14:5). **If Paul wouldn't bind a conscience on days, who may?**
Unity matters — if everyone decided individually, the congregation would splinter. The faithful slave keeps worship clean worldwide, and I'm grateful for that direction.

But watch what that trades away: Colossians 2:16 says 'let NO ONE judge you in respect of a festival' — and a judicial committee for celebrating Christmas is precisely someone judging you about a festival. Unity that Romans 14 builds is agreement to differ in love, not identical calendars under penalty. Here's my open door, and it's the whole point: **come to no service, sign nothing — just bring your family for dinner on the 25th, and see whether what happens at our table looks like sun worship or like gratitude for a Savior.** You'll be welcomed, not recruited.
